• *Vegetarian Pad Krapow* (no egg, no chicken)
• *Vegetarian Satay* (tofu skewers, peanut sauce) | | **Baan Thai** | 3000 W Irving Park Rd, Chicago, IL 60647 | (312) 555‑3456 | • *Vegetarian Panang Curry* (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• *Vegetarian Pad Kee Mao* (no egg, no pork)
• *Vegetarian Mango Sticky Rice* (dessert) | | **Thai Orchid** | 4000 W 31st St, Chicago, IL 60625 | (312) 555‑7890 | • *Vegetarian Tom Kha Soup* (no fish sauce, uses vegetable broth)

• *Vegetarian Green Papaya Salad* (no fish sauce, uses lime juice) | ### How to choose | Factor | Why it matters | Suggested pick | |--------|----------------|----------------| | **Proximity to you** | Shorter travel time means more time to enjoy your meal. | Use Google Maps or a navigation app to filter by distance. | | **Menu variety** | A larger vegetarian menu gives you more options. | Thai Basil or Siam Thai Bistro. | | **Ambiance** | If you’re looking for a quiet dinner or a lively spot. | Thai House (more casual) vs. Thai Orchid (more upscale). | | **Price range** | Budget-friendly vs. fine dining. | Thai Basil (mid‑range) vs. Thai Orchid (higher end). | ### Quick tips for ordering 1. **Ask for “no egg” or “no fish sauce”** – many dishes contain eggs or fish sauce by default. 2. **Request “tofu” instead of meat** – tofu is a common vegetarian protein in Thai cuisine. 3. **Check for “vegetable broth”** – especially for soups like Tom Yum or Tom Kha. 4. **Look for “no peanuts”** – if you’re allergic, ask for a version without peanuts or peanut sauce.
